My Price is My Life | Setting Sail with Whistleblower Jodi O’Malley and James O’Keefe Episode #4

Whistleblower Jodi O’Malley comes aboard the Lucky Charm III to share what her life’s been like since she heroically exposed how the federal government was handling (and allegedly hiding) adverse reactions to the COVID-19 vaccine.

In 2021, Jodi was a nurse at the Phoenix Indian Medical Center, a facility under the U.S. Department of Health and Human Services (HHS). She tells James how the Holy Spirit prompted her to hit “record” while her concerned colleagues, including physicians, were discussing patients they believed were suffering adverse effects from the vaccine, reactions that weren't being formally reported. Thus, igniting Jodi’s ongoing advocacy in nursing.

Jodi also shares other challenging moments in her life that strengthened her faith and trust in God, leading her to the work and mission she’s tackling now.

Multiple vulnerabilities in the Secure/Multipurpose Internet Mail Extensions (S/MIME) decryption functionality of Cisco Secure Email could allow an unauthenticated, remote attacker to recover plain text from encrypted email messages.
These vulnerabilities are due to insufficient validation of message integrity. An attacker could exploit these vulnerabilities by using a machine-in-the-middle technique to intercept and modify traffic between email gateways. A successful exploit could allow the attacker to obtain plaintext content from the encrypted communication.

There are no workarounds that address these vulnerabilities.

In the Name of God, the Most Compassionate, the Most Merciful

The Statute mandated the Agency to accelerate and enlarge the contribution of atomic energy to peace, health and prosperity, and to facilitate access by Member States to technical, scientific and technological assistance. Accordingly, technical assistance, the transfer of knowledge and technology, and capacity-building constitute core elements of the Agency’s Statutory responsibilities. They shall be provided without any discrimination and free from political considerations.
​
Nevertheless, unilateral sanctions and other restrictive measures have systematically impeded realization of these objectives. For decades, such unlawful measures constrained Iran’s ability to fully benefit from technical assistance, the transfer of knowledge and technology, and capacity-building.
​
Such measures run counter to the inalienable right of States for the peaceful uses of nuclear energy. Moreover, they contravene the obligations of developed States Parties to the NPT “to cooperate in contributing”, and “to the further development of the applications of nuclear energy for peaceful purposes, especially in the territories of non-nuclear-weapon States Party to the Treaty, with due consideration for the needs of the developing areas of the world.”
​
In discharging its responsibilities, the Agency is expected to seriously consider and duly address the impact of such restrictive measures on Member States. The policy making organs of the Agency must call for the termination of such sanctions and restrictions.
​
Distinguished Delegates
